title: Impact of Class Size Cap Policy on Reading Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The causal method I recommend for this analysis is the Differences-in-Differences (DID) approach. This method is suitable because we are interested in estimating the causal effect of a class size cap policy on students' reading scores by comparing the changes in scores between treated and untreated schools before and after the policy implementation. The key assumption here is the "parallel trends" assumption, which posits that, in the absence of the treatment, the difference in outcomes between the treated and control groups would have remained constant over time.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)

# Read the CSV file
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s45_data.csv")

# Fit a DID regression model
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)

# Print the summary of the DID model
summary(did_model)

# Extract and print the coefficient for the interaction term (treat_x_post)
did_coefficient <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
cat("DID Estimate for treat_x_post (impact of policy on reading scores):", did_coefficient, "\n")

# Perform a robustness check by adding a school-level fixed effect
robust_did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post + factor(unit_id), data = data)

# Print the summary of the robustness check model
summary(robust_did_model)

# Extract and print the robustness check coefficient for the interaction term (treat_x_post)
robust_did_coefficient <- coef(robust_did_model)["treat_x_post"]
cat("Robustness Check - DID Estimate for treat_x_post:", robust_did_coefficient, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect that the implementation of the class size cap policy would have a positive effect on reading scores, as smaller class sizes are generally believed to lead to more personalized attention and better educational outcomes. The approximate magnitude of the impact could range from small to moderate positive changes in reading scores measured in standard deviation units, depending on the baseline school performance and any additional confounding factors not captured in the dataset. However, precise numerical estimates will emerge from the empirical model outputs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Comparative analysis of reading scores before and after the policy in treated and untreated schools.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The class size cap policy resulted in a decrease in reading scores.
